source.title: Learning Rate Adaptation for Differentially Private Learning

record.tranche_reason: Applies learning-rate adaptation to differentially private SGD and reports test accuracy on MNIST and CIFAR-10; this is a new setting for optimizer/generalization comparisons.
record.gate_note: Reports test-accuracy comparisons among ADADP, DP-Adam, and DP-SGD, plus a private selection baseline. These results bear on V4's optimizer comparison. Architecture, batch-size, regularization, width, sharpness, memorization, and random-label claims are not tested. Numerical results in Figures 1, 3, and 4 are only described qualitatively in the text; Table 1 reports numeric results for a private-selection comparison.
record.test_reason: The study invokes Wilson et al.'s generalization finding to motivate learning-rate adaptation for SGD, but reports its proposed method's performance against DP-Adam, DP-SGD and private selection. It does not directly compare Adam with SGD under V4's tuning conditions. Comparing both against ADADP does not establish their relative generalization performance.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that their private learning-rate adaptation method performs competitively with tuned optimization methods without tuning its learning rate, and offers benefits over private meta-selection. They also demonstrate competitive performance in private variational inference.
record.recipe_differences: Differentially private learning-rate adaptation; uses DP-SGD gradients and evaluates test accuracy under privacy constraints rather than comparing the standard non-private optimizer settings in V4.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary with dataset and DP noise level; the DP-SGD comparison fixes a learning rate tuned at sigma=2.0 and reports advantages for sigma=4.0, 6.0, and 8.0. For DP-Adam, comparisons use best and second-best grid learning rates.

fits_no_version.finding: ADADP is competitive with best-grid DP-Adam on MNIST and CIFAR-10 and outperforms second-best-grid DP-Adam on MNIST.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Private learning-rate adaptation can achieve competitive test accuracy without a learning-rate grid search.

fits_no_version.finding: At noise sigma 4, 6 and 8, ADADP outperforms DP-SGD using a learning rate selected at sigma 2.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Learning-rate adaptation can improve private-training performance when the noise level changes and the baseline learning rate is transferred without retuning.

fits_no_version.finding: ADADP obtains mean CIFAR-10 accuracy 0.6349 in one training run; private selection at gamma 2^-8 obtains 0.6368 with 224.30 runs on average.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Private learning-rate adaptation can approach private hyperparameter-selection accuracy with substantially fewer training runs.

record.code_released: Code for the experiments is provided in the supplementary material; URL not stated.
record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics (AISTATS 2020), Proceedings of the 23rd International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics, PMLR Volume 108.
record.problems: The optimizer comparisons are in a differentially private setting, limiting direct comparison with the version's general claim. Several comparisons are described only qualitatively from figures, with no numerical values or uncertainty stated. In the DP-SGD comparison, its learning rate is tuned at sigma=2.0 and then compared at higher noise levels.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label versus random-label held-out performance.
Width beyond interpolation and its effect on test error.
Matched convolutional versus fully connected comparisons and the role of local connectivity.

Direct adaptive-optimizer versus SGD generalization comparisons under limited or broader tuning, training-performance comparisons, weight-decay changes, switching optimizers and language-model results.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove a large-batch penalty.
Effects of adding or removing dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.
Removing highly memorized examples versus random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: The supplied text provides no direct DP-Adam-versus-DP-SGD result or training-loss comparison. Separate comparisons against ADADP cannot justify either of the record's V4 support labels.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and generalization on natural labels.
Width sweep beyond interpolation and test error.
Non-private training, SGD or momentum comparisons, broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, switching from Adam to SGD, and word-level language models.
Large versus small batches under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and other generalization measures.
Removing memorized examples and measuring test-accuracy effects.

rows.subject: feedforward neural network with 2 hidden layers with 256 hidden units
rows.operation_detail: Compared DP-Adam and ADADP test accuracy at matched noise levels; Adam used best and second-best initial learning rates from a grid.

conditions.value: ADADP; Adam best; Adam second best

rows.baseline: DP-Adam with best or second-best initial learning rate, sought from the stated grid.
rows.value: ADADP is described as competitive with learning-rate-optimised Adam and better than Adam with the second best learning rate.
rows.note: Qualitative comparison only; no exact figure values are stated in the text.
rows.check: Proposed-method performance comparison, not evidence that adaptive optimizers generalize worse than SGD. The ADADP recipe includes adaptation followed by fixed-rate decay after the first 50 epochs; its competitiveness with DP-Adam cannot establish V4.

rows.subject: neural network with two convolutional layers followed by three fully connected layers
rows.operation_detail: Compared DP-Adam and ADADP test accuracy at matched noise levels; Adam used best and second-best initial learning rates from a grid.

conditions.value: ADADP; Adam best; Adam second best

rows.baseline: DP-Adam with best or second-best initial learning rate, sought from the stated grid.
rows.value: ADADP is described as competitive with learning-rate-optimised Adam.
rows.note: CIFAR-100 pretraining of convolutional layers is stated; differentially private optimization is carried out only for fully connected layers. Exact figure values are not stated in the text.
rows.check: Proposed-method performance comparison, not a direct Adam-versus-SGD test. Correct parameter count to approximately 10^6, not 106. Convolutional layers are pretrained on CIFAR-100; only fully connected layers receive private optimization.

rows.subject: feedforward neural network with 2 hidden layers with 256 hidden units
rows.operation_detail: Compared ADADP with DP-SGD at several noise levels, using DP-SGD learning rate tuned in the sigma=2.0 case.
rows.baseline: DP-SGD with fixed learning rate tuned in the sigma=2.0 case.
rows.value: For sigma=4.0, 6.0, and 8.0, ADADP finds an appropriate learning rate and gives better results than DP-SGD.
rows.note: The text states the comparative result; exact plotted values are not given.
rows.check: ADADP outperforming DP-SGD after changing noise levels measures adaptation to a transferred learning rate, not V4's adaptive-optimizer generalization claim. The stated advantage concerns sigma 4, 6 and 8; sigma 2 is the tuning reference.

rows.subject: neural network with two convolutional layers followed by three fully connected layers
rows.operation_detail: Compared ADADP with DP-SGD at several noise levels, using DP-SGD learning rate tuned in the sigma=2.0 case.
rows.baseline: DP-SGD with fixed learning rate tuned in the sigma=2.0 case.
rows.value: For sigma=4.0, 6.0, and 8.0, ADADP finds an appropriate learning rate and gives better results than DP-SGD.
rows.note: CIFAR-100 pretraining of convolutional layers is stated; differentially private optimization is carried out only for fully connected layers. Exact plotted values are not given.
rows.check: Proposed-method comparison against DP-SGD whose learning rate was tuned at sigma 2, with advantages stated at sigma 4, 6 and 8; this does not establish V4. Correct parameter count to approximately 10^6. Private optimization applies only to the fully connected layers.

rows.subject: not stated
rows.operation_detail: Compared ADADP against the private selection algorithm of Liu and Talwar using CIFAR-10 test data as validation for private selection.

conditions.value: same (epsilon, delta)-privacy for training dataset; validation privacy accounted for in private selection

rows.measure: Mean test accuracy; standard deviation of test accuracy; mean number of 100-epoch training runs per evaluation
rows.baseline: Private selection algorithm at each stated gamma value.
rows.uncertainty: Standard deviations are reported as listed in value.
rows.note: The comparison is of a private selection algorithm and ADADP's performance/compute cost; the model subject is not specified. It does not measure an optimizer generalization claim covered by V1–V8.
rows.check: Private hyperparameter-selection performance and computational cost do not test any version. This combines multiple selection conditions and measures rather than one result per condition and measure. The CIFAR-10 network is identifiable from Section 5.1.
